column2: DEFER severity=LOW — scripts/analysis/backlog-brief.mjs:15 "const sectionFlags = createRequire(import.meta.url)('../lib/review-template.js')" — this const is dead: nothing in the file ever prints the --section flags (the output names only ${ctxRel} and ${ctxSha} on the "Review (output only)" line, and the live one is backlog-lane.mjs:181), so the comment on :14 ("the committed context file is passed to the review tool with one --section per CONTEXT_SECTIONS entry") asserts behaviour this script does not implement — delete the const, or emit the flags in the review line so the claim on :14 is true — no reader of this file can tell the section flags are built elsewhere.

DEFER severity=LOW — scripts/analysis/backlog-brief.mjs:99 "const line = all[k - 1].slice(0, 4000);" — a document line longer than 4000 characters is cut silently and the block header still reads "lines ${from}-${last} of ${all.length}" with no cut note, while the range cut is marked "(cut at 12 KB)" — the reviewer takes the block as verbatim, so mark the line cut (or split the long line) the way the range cut is marked.

DEFER severity=LOW — scripts/analysis/backlog-brief.mjs:163 "fs.writeFileSync(path.join(root, ctxRel), ctx);" — neither this call nor the mkdirSync on :162 is guarded, so a read-only or permission-denied review dir throws an uncaught stack trace instead of the one-line die() the rest of the file uses and can leave a partial context file — wrap both in try/catch and die with the path and e.code.

DEFER severity=LOW — scripts/analysis/backlog-lane.mjs:37 "if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,31}$/.test(lane)) refuse(" — a malformed lane name is reported through refuse() (exit 3) although the header on :14 says "Usage errors exit 2" and the refusal list on :13 does not include the lane name, while the sibling value checks for --task (:36), --date (:40) and --stage (:51) use usage() — call usage() here too, because an orchestrator that branches on the exit code treats a typo as a launch refusal that may need the undo command.

DEFER severity=LOW — scripts/analysis/backlog-lane.mjs:77 "const letterOf = milestoneLetter(board, t.fm.milestone);" — the milestone group letter is derived twice: this call feeds resolveTask({...letter: letterOf}), and :175 re-parses it independently ("const letter = /\[([^\]]+)\]\s*$/.exec(String(msTitle ?? ''))?.[1];") for spec.groups ([letter ?? 'F']) — if the two parses ever disagree the rule lists are resolved for one group while the brief names another, so derive the letter once and reuse the value.

DEFER severity=LOW — scripts/analysis/backlog-lane.mjs:238 "} catch (e) { fail('write', { stderr: String(e && e.message) }); }" — this catch covers the worktree add, both node_modules links, the spec read, the JSON.parse of a caller --spec and brief.mjs, so every one of those failures is logged "FAILED at write" and exits 1, including an unreadable or malformed --spec that the header (:14) lists as an input refusal (exit 3) — catch per step, or pass the step name into fail, so the log line names what actually failed.

DEFER severity=NIT — .claude/review-templates/README.md:165 "the other four lens templates still carry the plan placeholder twice in their own prose" — each of the four templates in this same change (lens-code-review.md, lens-error-paths.md, lens-security.md, lens-ux.md) carries one literal {{PLAN}} and one {{SPECS}}, so the stated doubling no longer exists and callers who size a diff part from this note (38000 characters with a 33000 character pack) trim material for no reason — correct the note to the single-placeholder size.

DEFER severity=MED — scripts/analysis/proof-slice.mjs:146 "head: spawnSync('git', ['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], { cwd: REPO, encoding: 'utf8' }).stdout.trim()," — when git cannot be spawned `.stdout` is null and `.trim()` throws a TypeError at `main`'s default-argument evaluation, so the intended guard at line 156 never runs and the user gets a stack instead of the exit-2 message — read the result first and use `.stdout ?? ''` (or test `status`/`error`) so `!io.head` is what fails.

DEFER severity=LOW — scripts/analysis/gates/generated-docs.mjs:134 "const detail = violations.length" — this whole summary string (and the only `rows.filter(isRetired)` call) is computed and then neither returned nor printed, the JSDoc return at line 113 does not include it — either return it as `detail` and print it in `main`, or delete the block.

DEFER severity=LOW — scripts/analysis/proof-slice.mjs:29 "export function timeoutMsFromVariable(value) {" — neither this function nor `TIMEOUT_VARIABLE` (line 27) has a caller in the file; the only timeout source is the literal at line 22 "const DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 120000;" — wire it into `realIo.run` from `gateVariable(TIMEOUT_VARIABLE)`, or drop the export with the comment, so it is not dead until registration.

DEFER severity=LOW — scripts/analysis/gates/generated-docs.mjs:170 "const live = new Set(liveGeneratedDocs(repoRoot));" — `--report` calls the listing with no try/catch, so a missing or unreadable dir throws a stack trace, while the gate path at lines 124-128 records the same failure as a `listing` violation — wrap the call and print the listing error instead of throwing.

DEFER severity=NIT — scripts/analysis/proof-slice.mjs:55 "for (const k of ['waits', 'expect']) {" — the argv-only rule is enforced for `waits` and `expect` but not for `timeoutMs`, so a `timeoutMs` on a suite or notbuilt row passes `checkSpec` and is silently ignored by `commandRow` — add `timeoutMs` to the same argv-only guard.

DEFER severity=NIT — scripts/analysis/proof-slice.mjs:62 "if (r?.notbuilt !== undefined && (typeof r.notbuilt !== 'object' || r.notbuilt === null)) problems.push(" — an array passes this test, so `notbuilt: []` is then rejected with the misleading "notbuilt.blockedBy must be an array of task ids" — add `|| Array.isArray(r.notbuilt)` so the type error is reported as one.

DEFER severity=MED — scripts/lib/review-template.js:138 "return (fs.existsSync(dir) ? fs.readdirSync(dir).filter((f) => /^context-r\d+\.md$/.test(f)).length : 0) + 1;" — the next round number is a file COUNT, not the highest N, so after any gap (an aborted round, or a hand-removed context-r1.md) it returns a number that already exists and the brief overwrites that round's context file, breaking the per-round evidence the review stamps — fix: Math.max(0, ...the Ns found) + 1.

DEFER severity=MED — scripts/analysis/rule-lists.mjs:558 "try { p = buildLensInputs({ id: l.id, list: def, root, material: 'x'.repeat(NOMINAL), templateFile: tmpl }).length; } catch { p = 0; }" — a bare catch swallows every failure (a missing .claude/review-templates/lens-compliance.md, a render or room error) and the cell then prints "does not fit", so the real cause is never logged and a missing template reads as a size problem in the generated page — fix: let the error through, or put e.message in the cell.

DEFER severity=LOW — scripts/hooks/check-task-files.mjs:20 "function globToRegex(g) {" — the Files glob grammar now has two implementations, this local one and the shared one imported at scripts/analysis/rule-lists.mjs:25 "import { globToRegExp, matchesAny } from './mcbylaws/paths.mjs';", so one Files entry can be in scope for the commit hook and match no row at launch (or the reverse), and the header's reason ("package.json has no glob library") is stale — rationale: reuse globToRegExp so one matcher fix reaches both.

DEFER severity=LOW — scripts/deepseek-review.js:39 "if (!process.env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY) {" — the module-level key check runs before main(), so --dry-run and the help text exit 1 without a key, contradicting the flag's own contract in the help "Print the messages as one DRY-RUN line instead of calling the API" — rationale: move the key check after the help and dry-run branches, or into callDeepSeek.

DEFER severity=LOW — scripts/deepseek-review.js:94 "if (text) console.log(text);" — on a timeout the partial answer is printed here and then printed again by the caller ("console.log(lensResult.text);"), so the same partial text lands twice in stdout and in any file a caller writes from it — rationale: drop this line and let the caller print, or return no text on abort.

DEFER severity=LOW — scripts/lib/review-template.js:77 "return userTemplate.replace(/\{\{(PLAN|SPECS|DATA_CONTEXT)\}\}/g, (_m, key) => values[key]);" — a caller that omits plan or specs gets the literal string "undefined" substituted, which contradicts the docstring "Missing values are NOT silently substituted — the caller passes the literal fallback string" — rationale: throw when plan or specs is undefined; no current caller is hit, so no live defect.

DEFER severity=MED — src/tests/backlog/backlog-lane.logic.test.ts "const ok = run('node', [SCRIPT, ...f.args, '--dry-run', '--rule-lists', fake], { env: { ...ID, RULE_LISTS_ALLOW_OVERRIDE: '1' } }); expect(ok.stderr).not.toMatch(/--rule-lists/);" — a spawned CLI whose status and first line are never asserted, so a crash inside the override path passes the test, which contradicts the file's own stated rule at "Every spawned-CLI test first asserts the exit status and the first output line before any absence assertion (R-CP, 124a:296)" — assert expect(ok.status).toBe(0) and an output line before the absence check.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/backlog/check-task-files.logic.test.ts "expect(check(a.d).status, check(a.d).stderr).toBe(0);" — the hook is spawned twice, so the diagnostic message can come from a different run than the status being asserted, and any side effects happen twice — capture one result: const r = check(a.d); expect(r.status, r.stderr).toBe(0).

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/backlog/backlog-brief-context.logic.test.ts "expect(section(ctxOf(d, task), 'Document sections')).toMatch(/docs\/missing\.md.*not readable|not found/i);" — the alternation splits the whole pattern, so any occurrence of "not found" anywhere in the section satisfies it and the test does not prove the missing file is named — group the alternatives: /docs\/missing\.md.*(?:not readable|not found)/i.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/backlog/backlog-lane.logic.test.ts "const file = path.join(dir, fs.readdirSync(dir).find((n) => n.startsWith(f.task))!);" — the non-null assertion hides a real null, so a failed match surfaces as path.join(undefined) TypeError far from the cause, and the same line is repeated in the T4 test — assert the found name first or throw with f.task in the message.

DEFER severity=NIT — src/tests/backlog/backlog-lane.logic.test.ts "return { ...f, rev: path.join(f.base, 'rev') };" — the rev field and its PF type member are never read by any test in the file, dead fixture data — delete the field and return Fx.

DEFER severity=NIT — src/tests/backlog/backlog-lane.logic.test.ts "const extra = spec.extra.join('\n') as string;" — the cast is a no-op because join already returns string, and it papers over spec being any from JSON.parse, so a wrong shape only fails later at .join — drop the cast and type the parsed JSON.

DEFER severity=NIT — src/tests/backlog/backlog-lane.logic.test.ts "console.log(`ATTACK 11: REFUSED: ${r.stderr.trim().slice(0, 200)}`);" — leftover debug print in a test body, it asserts nothing — remove it or fold the text into the refusal assertion message.

DEFER severity=NIT — src/tests/backlog/review-templates.logic.test.ts "expect(a).toBeGreaterThan(0);" — indexOf is used as a presence check, so a match at index 0 would fail the test though the string is present — use toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0).

DEFER severity=MED — src/tests/backlog/rule-lists-table.logic.test.ts:359 "for (const f of [...SPECS, 'mobile/x.ts, docs/specs/02-web-admin/128_surface_standard_policy.md']) handbookOnly(lists(f), f);" — two paths are glued into one `--files` argument (everywhere else `lists()` takes one path), so either resolve splits on comma and this entry only duplicates checks already made on line 342 ('mobile/x.ts') and on SPECS (which already contains 128), or it does not split and the test dies at the `expect(r.status).toBe(0)` in the `lists` helper (line 15) — split it into two array entries, or drop it, it adds no coverage either way.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/backlog/rule-lists-table.logic.test.ts:193-195 "run('git', ['-c', 'user.email=t@t', '-c', 'user.name=t', 'commit', '-qm', 'x'], { cwd: d });" — the three git calls' exit status is discarded, so a failed init/add/commit leaves the temp tree uncommitted with no error logged and the failure surfaces later as a confusing resolve result — assert `run(...).status === 0` and include its stderr in the message.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/backlog/rule-lists-table.logic.test.ts:172 "const text = t.$comment.join('\\n');" — `$comment` is an unchecked `as` cast to `string[]`, so if the JSON carries a string `$comment` this throws a TypeError instead of failing an assertion, and the "proved by" check silently disappears — guard with `expect(Array.isArray(t.$comment)).toBe(true)` or normalise with `[].concat(t.$comment)`.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/backlog/rule-lists-table.logic.test.ts:271 "fs.mkdirSync(path.join(d, 'mcbylaws'));" — non-recursive mkdir inside a helper called many times in one test run (S1 alone calls it three times), which only works if `tmp('eng')` returns a fresh directory per call; cannot see helpers.ts, so if `tmp` is stable per key the second call throws EEXIST — pass `{ recursive: true }`.

DEFER severity=NIT — src/tests/backlog/rule-lists-table.logic.test.ts:117 "const four = ['surface-126', 'surface-128', 'surface-135', 'surface-136'];" then ":120" "for (const l of four.slice(0, 3))" — the variable called `four` holds the positive id (surface-136) in its last slot, so the negative loop must be sliced; anyone extending the loop to `four` breaks the `toContain('surface-136')` assertion two lines above — name the negatives (NOT_ATTACHED) and keep surface-136 in its own const.

DEFER severity=NIT — src/tests/backlog/rule-lists-table.logic.test.ts:11 "type Res = { lists: { id: string; rows: string[] }[] };" — `rows` is declared on the resolve result type and never read by any assertion, a cast field with no consumer — drop it so the type matches what the tests actually use (id only, plus `exempt` where needed).

DEFER severity=MED — src/tests/backlog/rule-lists.logic.test.ts "expect((m.parseLensInput(cut) as unknown as { ok: boolean }).ok).toBe(false);" — the file's own declared type says parseLensInput returns '{ listPart: string; id: string } | null', so this line reads a field that type does not have and the 'as unknown as' casts past the null case — add 'ok: boolean' to the declared result (or assert the call returns null on a shortened part) and drop the double cast.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/backlog/rule-lists.logic.test.ts:50 "const res = JSON.parse(r.stdout) as Res;" — the status is not checked before parsing, so a refused resolve (exit 3) surfaces as a JSON SyntaxError and the real stderr is discarded — put 'expect(r.status, r.stderr).toBe(0)' first, as every neighbouring resolve test does.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/backlog/rule-lists.logic.test.ts "?.[1] as string; (const filesLineOf = (n: number) => /^Files: (.*)$/m.exec(...)" — the 'as string' hides that the match can be undefined and that a wrapped Files line is cut at its first line, so resolvedIds receives 'undefined' or a partial path and the failure lands far from the cause — match, assert the capture, and throw naming the task id.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/backlog/rule-lists.logic.test.ts:269 "it('a big list is split by its own headings: every part carries the material, parts together hold every list line, none over the bound'" — the body never asserts the bound, while the V2.WHOLE tests do 'expect(t.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(max)' — add the per-part length assertion so the stated claim is enforced.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/backlog/rule-lists.logic.test.ts:280 "it('a split of a long single heading list falls to its deeper headings, and a section that cannot fit is refused naming list and section'" — only the refusal half runs (status 1 on list 'big' at 2600), the fall-to-deeper-headings half has no assertion — assert a successful split of a long single-heading section at a bound that fits, or rename the test.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/backlog/rule-lists.logic.test.ts "it('control: with no GIT_* set, a directory that is not a repository is refused (git ls-files failed), not answered from another repo'" — the premise in the name is never established: nothing unsets GIT_DIR, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_WORK_TREE and nothing proves tmp('norepo') sits outside a work tree — delete the three variables for the duration and restore them in a finally.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/backlog/rule-lists.logic.test.ts "const rt = createRequire(import.meta.url)(path.join(ROOT, 'scripts/lib/review-template.js'));" — require() yields any, so rt.extractSections, rt.CONTEXT_SECTIONS and rt.substitutePlaceholders are unchecked and a rename in that module leaves 'sel' undefined while the room assertion can still pass — type the module shape with an 'as' like the other dynamic imports in this file.
DEFER severity=NIT — src/tests/backlog/rule-lists.logic.test.ts:73 "expect(pipe).not.toContain('mobile-100');" — this cannot fail once line 72's exact toEqual pins the whole array — drop it.

DEFER severity=MED — src/tests/proof-slice.db.test.ts:20 "afterAll(async () => { await pool.end().catch(() => undefined); });" — the close error is swallowed with no log, and `pool` is dereferenced even when `beforeAll` (line 19) threw before assigning it, so a setup failure is reported as `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'end')` instead of its real cause — guard with `if (pool) await pool.end().catch((e) => console.error('proof-slice db: pool.end failed', e))` so the original beforeAll error is not masked.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/proof-slice.db.test.ts:34 "expect(timeoutMsFromVariable(rows[0].variable_value)).toBe(entry!.default);" — unlike the first `it` (line 24 "expect(rows, `${TIMEOUT_VARIABLE} is not registered in logic_variables`).toHaveLength(1)"), this case never asserts the row count, so a missing row throws a TypeError on `rows[0].variable_value` rather than naming the unregistered variable — add the same `toHaveLength(1)` guard before indexing.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/review-template.logic.test.ts:153 "return fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'review-notes-'));" — every test in this describe creates a temp dir and nothing removes it, unlike the sibling review-lens-template.infra.test.ts which pushes to `tmpDirs` and pops it in `afterEach` — collect the dirs and remove them in an `afterEach(() => fs.rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }))`.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/review-lens-template.infra.test.ts:28 "env: { PATH: process.env.PATH, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY: 'test-key-not-real' } as unknown as NodeJS.ProcessEnv," — the double cast is unnecessary (ProcessEnv's index signature already accepts `string | undefined`) and it silences the fact that `process.env.PATH` can be undefined, so the spawned CLI then fails with an ENOENT that reads like a product defect — drop the cast and use `PATH: process.env.PATH ?? ''` (or spread `...process.env`).

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/proof-slice.logic.test.ts:6 "The core is pure: `run` and `readFile` are injected, so no test below spawns a process." — the D10 case in the same file does spawn one: "mod.realIo().run(['node', '-e', \"process.stdout.write('x'.repeat(20 * 1024 * 1024))\"], { timeoutMs: 60000 })", so the header claim is stale and a 20 MiB child process now runs inside a `.logic.test.ts` whose name promises no process — update the header or move that case to an infra suite.

DEFER severity=LOW — src/tests/proof-slice.logic.test.ts:12 "const REPO = process.cwd();" — resolves the repo from the cwd while the neighbouring src/tests/hooks-composition.infra.test.ts:21 uses "const REPO_ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '../../');", so the data-file and task-file assertions silently read the wrong tree when the suite is started from another directory (`vitest --root`, a package-scoped run) — use `path.resolve(__dirname, '../..')` like the neighbour.

DEFER severity=MED — Spec 08 task-366 note 2 "puts the governing lists into the brief (READ each whole before planning) and runs the compliance lens once per list with the list pasted whole ahead of the plan or diff" — scripts/analysis/backlog-brief.mjs:183 "the output lens set and its commands are in the lens line of this brief" — the brief this script emits holds no lens line and no rule-list line (the out array, lines 168 to 191, carries neither, and sectionFlags built at line 16 is never used), so a lane following this brief is handed no compliance command and no governing list — the file's own header at lines 4 to 5 promises it prints "the review command", and the brief points at a section it does not contain; fix: print the per-list rule-lists.mjs lens-input and deepseek-review.js review commands, with the CONTEXT_SECTIONS --section flags taken from sectionFlags, before the Close step

DEFER severity=LOW — Spec 08 5.1 "Item-by-item, spec-clause → code-line, PASS/FAIL." — .claude/review-templates/lens-compliance.md:62 "at most 8 MET lines, only for clauses the change is most likely to break" — the format records an Unmet count and the met rule ids but no PASS/FAIL line per clause, so a binding clause that falls beyond the eight findings lines has no item-by-item outcome — on a list longer than eight binding clauses the seat's item-by-item record is incomplete; fix: reconcile Clauses checked and Unmet with the MET ids plus the BUG and DEFER lines so every clause has exactly one outcome

DEFER severity=MED — task-375 pasted AC "proof-slice-reads-its-limits-from-settings-D11-D10" — scripts/analysis/proof-slice.mjs:75 "const res = run(row.argv, { timeoutMs: row.timeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS });" — the command rows take their timeout from the typed constant DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (proof-slice.mjs:22) and the exported timeoutMsFromVariable has no caller in the file, so proof-slice does not read this limit from settings — when the variable is registered, pass gateVariable(TIMEOUT_VARIABLE) through timeoutMsFromVariable into realIo's run instead of the constant.

DEFER severity=MED — task-363 pasted AC "exit-2-on-an-unwritable-out-dir" — scripts/analysis/proof-slice.mjs:160 "try { io.mkdir(outDir); } catch (e) { console.error(`proof-slice: cannot create --out ${outDir} (${e?.code ?? e?.message ?? 'error'})`); return 2; }" — mkdirSync with recursive:true returns cleanly when the directory already exists, so an existing but unwritable --out passes this arm and the first evidence writeFile throws uncaught (exit 1 with a stack), i.e. only a non-creatable path gets exit 2 — probe writability (fs.accessSync W_OK, or write and unlink a temp file) after mkdir and return 2 when it fails.

DEFER severity=MED — dated note 2026-11-20 (grounder round 5) "the task type and the lane assignee are read from the BOARD copy of the task file (found by task id on `refs/heads/wf2/board`, the ref the launch commit is searched on)" — scripts/analysis/backlog-lane.mjs:63 "const t = readItems(board).find((x) => x.id === taskId);" — the launcher reads the task from the board checkout's working tree, and its dirty check (backlog-lane.mjs:84 "filter((p) => !p.startsWith('backlog/')") lets uncommitted backlog/ edits stand, so an uncommitted type or milestone edit on the board checkout decides the launch gate and the resolved rule lists rather than the board ref copy the ruling pins — read type, assignee and the Files line from `git show refs/heads/wf2/board:<path>` with the origin fallback, the same copy the launch-commit search uses.

DEFER severity=LOW — task-366 dated note 2026-11-20 (2) "the path to rule-list table: data, not code, says which rule lists ... govern a touched path" — scripts/analysis/backlog-lane.mjs:74 "if (rlOpt && path.resolve(home(rlOpt)) !== path.resolve(DEFAULT_TABLE) && process.env.RULE_LISTS_ALLOW_OVERRIDE !== '1') refuse(...)" — the only launch-time check that the table is the repo's own is switched off by an environment variable no pasted ruling names, so a launch can be briefed from a narrower table — drop the env arm or restrict it to a test-only path that still refuses a table outside the repo.

DEFER severity=MED — task-410 dated note 2026-11-20 (2) "With no `--list` and a lens template it writes the same chunks for code-review, error-paths, ux and security (the split the operator kept)" — scripts/analysis/backlog-lane.mjs:188 "the code-review, error-paths, ux and security lenses whose prompt would pass the bound use the same tool with their own template and no --list" — the brief conditions those four lenses on fitting the bound, so a lane reading it can skip them entirely for a change too large for the bound, where the ruling says the tool chunks the diff for them as it does for a rule list — state in the same sentence that lens-input chunks the diff at file boundaries for those four lenses too, never by hand, and file them as out-<lens>-pN.txt.

DEFER severity=NIT — pasted group scope "Tasks homed in this group: task-68, task-358, task-363, task-365, task-366, task-369, task-375, task-399, task-406, task-407, task-410, task-412, task-418, task-419, task-423, task-432, task-433" — scripts/analysis/backlog-lane.mjs:234 "const AGENT_MODEL = 'AGENT-MODEL: opus (RR-0385: set model \"opus\" on the Agent call that takes the BRIEF-FILE line below)';" — a model-split instruction and its printed line are added that no pasted clause or ruling names (task-436 is not in the pasted set) — keep it only if its ruling is pasted at the next review, otherwise list it as an out-of-scope addition with its ruling reference.

BUG severity=HIGH — task-366 note (2) "refuses a task with no Files line (a record-only task gets the queue lists)" — scripts/analysis/rule-lists.json:231 "  \"no_files_default\": { \"types\": [\"record\"], \"row\": \"queue-records\" }" — the default row attaches nothing (":158 \"lists\": [],"), so a record-only task now resolves to no queue list at all, and the only cited authority for the drop is task-448 (RR-0418), which is not among the pasted rulings — attach queue-137 and agents-s7-s11 to the queue-records row, or paste the ruling that turned them off

BUG severity=HIGH — task-366 note "(the surface specs 126, 127, 128 and the full Spec 135 rows go into the path table)" — scripts/analysis/rule-lists.json:146 "      \"lists\": [\"surface-136\", \"eng-all\"]," — surface-126, surface-127, surface-128 and surface-135 are still defined (":38" to ":41") but no row attaches any of them, so no touched surface path resolves to the four lists the operator's ruling put in the table — re-attach the four lists on the surfaces, mobile, specs-web-admin and surface-contract-routes rows, or paste the task-439 and task-448 rulings that removed them

DEFER severity=MED — operator 2026-11-20 "yes to McStorage and 1,2,3 yes as recommended" — scripts/analysis/rule-lists.json:133 "      \"lists\": []," — the storage row attaches no list and storage-doc16 (":36") is attached by no row, so a parcel or report-projection storage change resolves to no McStorage policy list, the row's why resting only on the unpasted task-448 — restore storage-doc16 on the storage row or paste the ruling that turned it off
